audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Yorick levels 2, 3 and first item and called levels 4-5 and 6 Skill, on a 47.25% matchup whose own why-strings say 'Kled dominates levels 1-4' and 'first-item Kled still out-duels you'.
audit.why: The mirror settled levels 2, 3, 4-5, 6 and First item as Kled with 2+ items to Yorick, and the packet chart agrees on rows 1-4. Every row except the last belongs to Kled: he wins mounted trades from level 1 and his dismount burst holds through the first item, while Yorick's only lead is the two-item side lane with Maiden.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 to Kled on both layers with ratings 3/3/3/3/4/4, 2+ items stays Yorick at 6/10; diff EVEN to HARD and diffRating 6/10 to 7/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1], [2] and [5] why-strings claimed Yorick spikes ('your core pattern starts now', 'Trinity Force is your spike') on rows that belong to Kled.
audit.why: Kled's spikes are Violent Tendencies from level 1-2 (four fast attacks on 13s), Bear Trap at 11s, and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! at 6 for engage plus a shield. Yorick's only spike that beats him is Maiden with two items in the side lane — the page's own late text says exactly that.
audit.corrected: Rewrote phases[1].why, phases[2].why, phases[3].why and phases[5].why to those spikes, plus whys[4] and whys[5] to match the corrected rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bear Trap was described only as 'his engage hook, dodge it' with no range, no cooldown and no mention that it yanks you in on a delay. Jousting and its return dash were absent entirely, as was Violent Tendencies' auto-reset.
audit.why: Bear Trap is 800 range on 11s at rank 1 and pulls you toward him after the shackle delay, so the escape happens after it hits, not before. Jousting is a 550 dash on 13s at rank 1 that he can recast back through you — Dark Procession creates terrain, which is the one tool that can deny that return. Violent Tendencies is an auto-reset, so his burst opens on an attack wind-up, not a visible cast. Dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions per Riot's text, which is what makes stripping Skaarl the real trade goal.
audit.corrected: All of it into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, dontsFull[1].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization and breakdown.late both push anti-heal as core against Kled.
audit.why: Nothing in Kled's kit carries a heal flag. His health comes back by remounting Skaarl at full courage, which Grievous Wounds does not touch — so the advice buys an item for an interaction that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Swapped the anti-heal line for Plated Steelcaps against Violent Tendencies' four attacks, and 'anti-heal stays core' for 'the split stays core'.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Bear Trap on a Rope's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: His window, not yours: dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions, so the only trade worth taking is the one that strips Skaarl.

edits.before: Trinity Force is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Bear Trap on a Rope's cooldown.
edits.after: Trinity Force closes the gap but he still out-duels you — take it to shove and split, not to fight him head-on.

edits.before: - Kled Bear Trap on a Rope: matchup-defining — His engage hook. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Bear Trap on a Rope: 11s at rank 1, 800 range — it yanks you in, so break line of sight or hold a wall. - Jousting: 13s at rank 1, and Dark Procession can block the return dash. - Violent Tendencies: 13s auto-reset.

edits.after: Start Doran's Blade + pot. Core: Trinity Force  (the all-purpose spike), then Hullbreaker; boots Plated Steelcaps. They blunt Violent Tendencies' four fast attacks.
